blindSummary:
This state/province shows the country's clearest border-checkpoint pattern of profiling gender-nonconforming presentation as a suspicion trigger for foreign infiltration. Three mass police sweeps in five months (Aug–Nov 2024) at a check post on an inter-city highway detained 15, 7 and 12 people respectively, with police reporting language explicitly framing trans identity as "disguised as third-gender" — a category of deception rather than personhood. The state/province shares an 856 km border with a neighbouring country. These are official state-actor operations with published counts, constituting a patterned enforcement practice directly facing any trans-presenting visitor crossing by land.

A large negative deviation from the country-wide average: while the country has no statute criminalising trans presence, this state/province's checkpoint regime converts gender-nonconforming appearance into an independently sufficient reason for detention and deportation proceedings. Compared with a neighbouring state/province, where the same script exists but is recorded in fewer, more isolated incidents, this state/province's three sweeps and explicit disguise framing make it the most concentrated instance of this visitor-facing harm in the country.

There is a constituted transgender welfare board (one of only 12 sub-national units nationwide to have one), but an information-disclosure investigation found most such boards to be leaderless, with no compliance mechanism or real power — this institutional presence does not offset active police profiling at the border.
